intent: vendor preset "Falling Sparks" (Smoke and Fire) — validate against its thumbnail

iterations.critique: The render has the correct black-background ember palette and the particles do drift downward between t1 and t4, but it reads as a tiny, sparse cluster of pixel-sized dots near the center rather than the visibly substantial falling-sparks shower expected from the preset thumbnail. Spark coverage, brightness, and apparent particle scale are all far too low; the short lifetime also keeps the falling trail compact.

The black background, fiery yellow/orange/red palette, and clearly downward motion from t1 to t4 now read as falling sparks. Density is improved, but the effect remains a narrow, centered vertical plume with very small dot-like particles. It lacks the broader, more substantial shower and longer descending field expected of the Falling Sparks thumbnail; the bright source cluster is also too compact relative to the frame.

The render now clearly reads as fiery falling sparks: it has a black background, dense yellow/orange/red embers, visible glow, and the t4 frame shows the particle mass descending. However, it remains a tight, centered column rather than the wider, more dispersed falling-sparks shower indicated by the preset thumbnail. The source and trail are still compact, with small bead-like particles and insufficient lateral spread; the field should occupy substantially more width and persist farther downward.

The render has the intended black backdrop, bright yellow/orange/red ember palette, dense emission, and a discernible downward shift from t1 to t4. However, it still reads as a narrow central column of soft bead-like particles rather than the broader, scattered falling-sparks shower of the preset thumbnail. The lateral field is too constrained and the visible trail remains relatively compact, with the lower portion crowding/cropping near the bottom instead of sustaining a more extended descending shower.

The render retains the correct black backdrop, dense warm fire palette, glow, and a visible downward progression from t1 to t4. However, it still reads as a compact, soft bead-like central plume instead of a broad field of individually falling sparks. At t4 the lower mass crowds into and clips at the bottom edge while the upper source remains narrow; the shower needs substantially more lateral distribution and less clustered particle scale.
